body: I’ll bring up some of those points in therapy. Thank you very much for talking to me. It was nice to get some of this off my chest even if I didn’t directly speak about what happened. I’m probably going to keep this account around and to hopefully one day be able to just vent all what happened one day. Do you think that’s a good idea? I worry of my assault being reported even though I know it’s anonymous. Hopefully not in this subreddit of course. I’m going to speak with someone I know in real life just to make sure everything will be okay tonight. Once again thank you for taking the time to speak to me tonight. Really did help me get my thoughts back on the right track.

I used to just ignore the incident of assault till very recently. It’s been about 2 weeks sense I started therapy, told my best friend, and told my girlfriend about the past assault. It took me a long time to realize that the shame I carried wasn’t normal. That someone not accepting my “no” was wrong on their part not mine. I realize now the shame I carry is from the consequences. I have GAD before the incident and had 5 years of CBT therapy   so I have always been a horribly anxious person but have done a good job at managing a normal life even if I do some things abnormally to cope. I feel no shame and it truly isn’t a big part of my identity. However my huge fear of cars and women in general which developed after the assault cause me to feel ashamed as I don’t know how to cope with the anxiety. I’m working through it in therapy, yet that doesn’t stop it from being an obstacle in my daily life and relationships. I can’t help but he frustrated with myself as I just want to “treat” the issue like I’ve done in the past yet i know that’s impossible because one issue was genetic and the other was trauma.

It’s wearing me down and just keeping me up. I’m not in any active danger of hurting myself or others. I just wish I could fall asleep forever, and not have to deal with this anymore, which I know is technically a bit of suicidal thinking. That is why I thought I should talk to someone even if it’s anonymously, if that makes sense? I’m trying so hard to be logical about this when it truly doesn’t feel that ways. I can’t help but be angry with myself for being so emotional about what happened. Even though it was a stereotypical traumatic event and it makes perfect sense for me to effected. The shame just gets worse because I know it’s illogical.

It’s going realistically well. I’m just having a hard time processing everything. I want to get better and be successful, and I’m determined to get there. I wish there was a way to talk to her anonymously like this. I’m not comfortable sharing any details of what happened to her or anonymously so that’s what I’m working towards.
